source: AWS EC2 on-demand, Linux, us-east-1, retrieved 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-14 from ec2instances.info (Vantage), which republishes the AWS Price List API
physical_core_hour_basis: c7i.xlarge $0.1785/h for 4 vCPUs = 2 physical cores (Intel Sapphire Rapids)
gpu_pricing_rule: Each measured GPU is priced as the cheapest AWS on-demand GPU with at least its memory capacity and bandwidth, so the measured performance is reachable on the priced card. GPU price = instance price minus its physical cores at physical_core_hour.
gpu_hour_basis: First server's RTX A6000 (48 GiB, 768 GB/s; AWS does not rent it) priced as an NVIDIA L40S (48 GiB, 864 GB/s): g6e.xlarge $1.861/h minus its 2 physical cores. The L4 and A10G have 24 GiB, half the A6000's memory, and are kept in gpu_alternatives as sensitivity prices.
gpu_hour_second_server_basis: Second server's RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GiB) priced as the same GPU in g7e.2xlarge, $3.36312/h minus its 4 physical cores. Used for the remote-GPU and remote-sharing runs.
break_even_basis: price at which 8 cores plus one GPU costs the same per write as native RocksDB on 32 cores (equal-cost campaign, untuned); above the L4, A10G and L40S, below the RTX PRO 6000
